results.title: 'France has some of the cleanest electricity in the world, but we're not using enough of it'
results.content: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Thierry Bros, energy & climate expert and Professor of Science and Economics at Sciences Po. As geopolitical conflicts unsettle global energy markets and governments struggle to reconcile climate commitments with economic and security imperatives, the answer lies in a fundamental reconsideration of the sequence of climate policy. "Electrification first," he argues, acknowledging that this "doesn't necessarily mean clean electricity." His argument is grounded in a critical assessment of international climate diplomacy and European energy policy. "We've seen many COPs, and they've all failed," he contends, questioning the effectiveness of ambitious targets that have yet to deliver the necessary structural transformation. Italy evacuates hundreds of schools after receiving email bomb threats

results.title: Pope Leo to end Argentina tour with outdoor mass before Peru 'homecoming'
results.content: Pope Leo will conclude his three-day visit to Argentina Wednesday with an outdoor mass expected to draw millions before continuing his tour of South America by travelling to Peru, where he once served as a missionary. The pontiff plans to deliver a speech in front of Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori, whose election earlier this year was marred ‌by fraud accusations and vote-counting delays.

results.content: Russia and Ukraine have resumed US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi for a second day, Kyiv's chief negotiator Rustem Umerov said on Wednesday.

results.title: French journalist Christophe Gleizes marks 500 days in Algerian jail
results.content: Having been detained for 500 days in an Algerian prison on charges of “glorifying terrorism”, French journalist Christophe Gleizes continues to serve a seven-year sentence despite an intense campaign by his family and friends and the football world. While awaiting a presidential pardon, his supporters are stepping up their media campaign to secure his release. FRANCE 24 spoke with his friend Pierre de la Saussay.

results.title: Second day of Web Summit cancelled as Storm Charles puts Portugal on high alert
results.content: Portuguese authorities strongly advised organisers of the Web Summit to cancel events this Wednesday because of risks of tidal flooding and severe disruption to public transport. Storm Charles is expected to be at its most dangerous on Wednesday afternoon, with winds reaching up to 120 km/h and potentially very dangerous wind gusts as well.

results.title: Africa: Ghana waste dump poses health, environmental 'crisis'
results.content: An acrid haze hung over a sprawling dump in Ghana's capital, Accra, as excavators gouged into mounds of smouldering rubbish. Thin plumes of black smoke curled from burning plastic and rubber, mingling with the rank odour of stagnant lagoon water.

results.title: Want to live on the moon? NASA opens recruitment for Artemis programme
results.content: NASA is expanding its astronaut corps for the first time in two years. As the US space agency grows its Artemis programme, recruitment is in progress for a brand-new class of space explorers who will train to "live and work beyond Earth".

results.title: US House blocks bid to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
results.content: The US House of Representatives turned aside a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday, halting an effort to remove the Pentagon chief for his conduct in office and his handling of the war in Iran. Story by Jack Pownall.

results.title: Spain’s general strike puts housing crisis at centre of upcoming elections
results.content: Millions of Spanish workers are striking Wednesday – the first general strike in 14 years – to demand action on a major housing crisis and the rising cost of living. The expected disruptions to public transport and the widespread closure of businesses come less than three weeks before a snap election that could bring the far right to power.

results.title: Teddy Riner candidacy 'illustrative of hunger for alternatives' to France's Le Pen or Mélenchon
results.content: As Teddy Riner throws his hat in the race for the French presidency, amid France's sociopolitical and economic crises, François Picard is pleased to welcome Lex Paulson, Director of Executive Programs at UM6P School of Collective Intelligence at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University.
